solutionReview.headline: Right {{h}} and up {{k}}: $({{x1}},{{y1}})$.
reasoning: $f(x-{{h}})$ shifts the graph {{h}} units right, and $+{{k}}$ shifts it {{k}} units up.
solutionReview.commonError: Shifting left for $x-{{h}}$; subtracting inside the function moves the graph right.

solutionReview.headline: The major axis is horizontal; go $a={{a}}$ right of the center: $({{xp}},{{k}})$.
reasoning: The center is $({{h}},{{k}})$. The larger denominator, ${{a2}}={{a}}^2$, is under the $x$-term, so the major axis is horizontal.
Major-axis vertices are {{a}} units left and right of the center, at the same $y$-value {{k}}.

act.prompt: The ellipse $\dfrac{(x {{nh|term}})^2}{{{a2}}}+\dfrac{(y {{nk|term}})^2}{{{b2}}}=1$ has $a>b$. Which point is a vertex on its major axis?

solutionReview.headline: The vertices are $a$ on each side of the center: {{answer}} apart.
reasoning: In $\frac{(x-h)^2}{a^2}-\frac{(y-k)^2}{b^2}=1$ the vertices are $a$ units left and right of the center.
solutionReview.commonError: Giving $a$ alone, which is the distance from the center to one vertex.

reasoning: The point $(-{{a}},{{b}})$ is {{a}} units left of the $y$-axis and {{b}} units above the $x$-axis.
Left and up is the upper-left region, Quadrant II (Quadrant I is upper right; the numbering goes counterclockwise).

$P$ is {{y}} units above the axis, so its image is {{y}} units below, at $({{x}},{{ny}})$.

solutionReview.headline: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals: -{{run}}/{{rise}}.
reasoning: Flip the fraction and change its sign: the negative reciprocal of {{rise}}/{{run}} is $-\frac{ {{run}} }{ {{rise}} }$.
Check: $\frac{ {{rise}} }{ {{run}} }\cdot\frac{ -{{run}} }{ {{rise}} }=-1$, as perpendicular slopes must multiply to $-1$.
